existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee to cover actual cost
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover its actual cost of providing a record; the fee must be approved by the entity's executive officer.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: (a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; also bounded by the soft 'reasonable' standard. Executive-officer approval is a structural sub-requirement (UT-0030).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: When compiling a record in a form other than normally maintained, actual costs may include staff time for compiling/formatting/tailoring, staff time for search/retrieval and direct administrative costs, and (for non-word-processing computer output) actual incremental cost plus a reasonable portion of formatting/administrative costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Entity compiles a record in a form other than normally maintained
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: When a governmental entity compiles a record in a form other than that normally maintained by the governmental entity, the actual costs under this section may include the following: (i) the cost of staff time for compiling, formatting, manipulating, packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record...; (ii) the cost of staff time for search, retrieval, and other direct administrative costs for complying with a request; and (iii) in the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer output other than word processing, the actual incremental cost of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with formatting or interfacing the information for particular users, and the administrative costs...

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Hourly charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An hourly staff-time charge may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: An hourly charge under Subsection (2)(a) may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the discretion of the custodian of records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Political subdivisions set fees by ordinance/policy
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Political subdivisions must establish records fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Political subdivisions shall establish fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: The municipal hook: the CITY supplies the actual fee schedule under the state's actual-cost ceiling (UT-0028).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may (and is encouraged to) fulfill a request without charge if release primarily benefits the public, the requester is the subject of/specified in the record, or the requester's legal rights are directly implicated and the requester is impecunious.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: One of the enumerated benefit/subject/impecunious conditions
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may fulfill a record request without charge and is encouraged to do so if it determines that: (a) releasing the record primarily benefits the public rather than a person; (b) the individual requesting the record is the subject of the record, or an individual specified in Subsection 63G-2-202(1) or (2); or (c) the requester's legal rights are directly implicated by the information in the record, and the requester is impecunious.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Denial of a fee waiver is separately appealable (UT-0040) and reviewed de novo (§ 63G-2-203(6)).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No fee for reviewing a record for disclosability
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted for search/retrieval staff time under 203(2)(a)(ii).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: (i) reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted by Subsection (2)(a)(ii);

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of staff time free
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent responding to a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Entity responds to a request under § 63G-2-204
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: ... (iii) the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fixed free allotment of 15 minutes. Exception in UT-0036.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Exception to free first quarter hour for repeat non-media requesters
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The free first quarter hour does not apply if the requester is not a Utah media representative AND previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the current request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Non-media requester filed a separate request within prior 10 days
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Notwithstanding Subsection (5)(b)(iii), a governmental entity is not prevented from charging a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204 if the person who submits the request: (i) is not a Utah media representative; and (ii) previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the date of the request to which the governmental entity is responding.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: 'Media representative' here (203(5)(a)) excludes blog/podcast/social-media requesters, unlike the broader publication/broadcast presumption in 204(5).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Fees expected to exceed $50, or prior invoiced fees unpaid
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: processing withheld until prepayment received ('before beginning to process a request')
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A governmental entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request if: (i) fees are expected to exceed $50; or (ii) after the government entity has sent an invoice, the requester has not paid fees from a previous request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Prepayment gate; the request enters a hold state until paid. Threshold value in UT-0038.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Prepayment may be required when fees are expected to exceed $50.
Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due must be returned to the requester.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Prepaid amount exceeds fees actually due
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due shall be returned to the requester.
